title: Global View - Live from Washington
audio: mp3/34. Global View - Live from Washington.mp3

segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: Welcome back to another great lesson here with EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到 EnglishPod 的另一个精彩课程。

segments.en: And today we're bringing you an upper intermediate lesson.
segments.zh: 今天，我们为您带来上级中级课程。

segments.en: A special lesson about the new president.
segments.zh: 关于新总统的特别教训。

segments.en: It's been a hot topic in the US, the new president elect, President Obama.
segments.zh: 这一直是美国的热门话题，新当选总统奥巴马总统。

segments.en: So today we're bringing you something that you might see at his inaugural address.
segments.zh: 所以今天我们为您带来一些您可能在他的就职演说中看到的东西。

segments.en: So Marco, can you explain this word, inaugural address?
segments.zh: 那么马可，你能解释一下这个词，就职演说吗？

segments.en: The inaugural address is the first speech the president gives at the ceremony when he is officially president.
segments.zh: 就职演说是总统在正式担任总统时发表的第一次演讲。

segments.en: So it's his first presidential speech.
segments.zh: 所以这是他的第一次总统演讲。

segments.en: So let's take a look at some other words that we're going to find in the dialogue today in vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 因此，让我们来看看我们将在今天的词汇预览中的对话中找到的其他一些词。

segments.en: On vocabulary preview today we have two words.
segments.zh: 在今天的词汇预览中，我们有两个词。

segments.en: The first one is swear in.
We'll see this word in its past tense in the dialogue, right?
segments.zh: 我们会在对话中看到这个词的过去时，对吧？

segments.en: So to swear someone in is to officially give that person a very important position.
segments.zh: 所以发誓某人是正式给那个人一个非常重要的位置。

segments.en: And our second word is oath.
segments.zh: 我们的第二个词是誓言。

segments.en: And oath goes hand in hand with swear in, right?
segments.zh: 誓言与宣誓就绪并肩作战，对吧？

segments.en: When you swear someone in, they make an oath.
segments.zh: 当你发誓某人时，他们会宣誓。

segments.en: An official promise to carry out the duties of that job.
segments.zh: 正式承诺履行该工作的职责。

segments.en: So they promise that they will do their job.
segments.zh: 所以他们承诺他们会做他们的工作。

segments.en: So now let's listen to our dialogue for a first time.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们第一次听我们的对话。

segments.en: Well, we're actually watching a news reporter on TV.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们实际上是在电视上观看新闻记者。

segments.en: She's in Washington and she's going to tell us all about what's happening.
segments.zh: 她在华盛顿，她会告诉我们发生了什么事。

segments.en: This is Madeline Wright for BCC News reporting live from Washington, DC, where very shortly the new president will deliver his inaugural address.
segments.zh: 这里是BCC新闻记者玛德琳·赖特，从华盛顿特区为您直播报道。新任总统很快就将发表就职演说。

segments.en: Just moments ago, the president was sworn into office following the United States Constitution.
segments.zh: 总统刚刚依照《美国宪法》宣誓就职。

segments.en: The president swore an oath to faithfully execute the office of the presidency.
segments.zh: 他宣誓将忠实履行总统职责。

segments.en: And what exactly is going on now, Madeline?
segments.zh: 玛德琳现在到底发生了什么？

segments.en: Well, Tom, true to American tradition, the band has just played Hail to the Chief and the president has been honored with a 21-gun salute.
segments.zh: 汤姆，按照惯例，乐队刚刚演奏了《向统帅致敬》，还鸣放了二十一响礼炮向总统致敬。

segments.en: Now we're waiting for the president to take the stage and deliver his speech.
segments.zh: 现在我们正在等待总统上台发表他的演讲。

segments.en: Tom, it's like the who's who of the political world here on Capitol Hill, with dignitaries representing several different countries.
segments.zh: 汤姆，国会山上政坛名流云集，还有来自多个国家的政要。

segments.en: What's the mood on the ground like, Madeline?
In a word, the mood here is electric.
segments.zh: 一句话，现场气氛热烈非凡。

segments.en: The excitement in the air is palpable.
segments.zh: 空气中洋溢的兴奋之情几乎触手可及。

segments.en: I've never seen a larger crowd here on Capitol Hill.
segments.zh: 我从没见过国会山上聚集这么多人。

segments.en: The audience is shouting, crying, and embracing each other.
On this, a most historic day, you can feel the hope and the excitement in the air.
segments.zh: 在这个最具历史意义的日子里，你可以感受到空气中的希望和兴奋。

segments.en: The 20th of January will go down in history as the...
segments.zh: 一月二十日将作为……载入史册。

segments.en: Oh, Tom, it looks like the president is about to begin.
segments.zh: 哦，汤姆，看起来总统即将开始。

segments.en: My fellow Americans, I stand before you today...
segments.zh: 我的美国同胞，我今天站在你面前...

segments.en: Okay, some technical problems at the inaugural address.
segments.zh: 好的，就职演说中的一些技术问题。

segments.en: Yeah, I certainly hope this doesn't happen.
segments.zh: 是的，我当然希望这不会发生。

segments.en: Well, if it does, you heard it first at EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果是这样，您首先在 Englishpod 上听到了它。

segments.en: Okay, let's take a look at Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们看看语言外卖。

segments.en: On Language Takeaway today, we're bringing you four words.
segments.zh: 在今天的语言外卖中，我们为您带来了四个词。

segments.en: We've got three examples that will show the meaning of this word.
segments.zh: 我们有三个例子来说明这个词的含义。

segments.en: Who's going to deliver the welcome speech?
I've been asked to deliver a presentation on the findings of our research project.
segments.zh: 我被要求就我们研究项目的结果发表演讲。

segments.en: Dr. Rosen is delivering a lecture on macroeconomics.
segments.zh: 罗森博士正在发表关于宏观经济学的讲座。

segments.en: So you wouldn't say say a speech, you would say deliver a speech.
segments.zh: 所以你不会说演讲，你会说发表演讲。

segments.en: The next word for Language Takeaway, the who's who.
segments.zh: 语言外卖的下一个词，名人录。

segments.en: So this is a funny expression, hey?
segments.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的表达，嘿？

segments.en: The who's who is the important people in a particular field, right?
segments.zh: 谁是特定领域的重要人物，对吧？

segments.en: So, for example, there was a party last night and the who's who of the film industry was there.
segments.zh: 所以，例如，昨晚有一个派对，电影业的名人录在那里。

segments.en: Whoa, so all the important stars and directors.
segments.zh: 哇，所以所有重要的明星和导演。

segments.en: So you would say the funeral was like a who's who of the political world.
segments.zh: 所以你会说葬礼就像一个政治世界的名人录。

segments.en: Okay, so all the important political figures were at this funeral.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以所有重要的政治人物都参加了这次葬礼。

segments.en: Let's move to our third word, Dignitaries.
segments.zh: 让我们转到我们的第三个词，政要。

segments.en: Okay, we have some great examples so you can understand what this word means.
segments.zh: 好的，我们有一些很好的例子，以便您可以理解这个词的含义。

segments.en: Several important dignitaries were present at the opening ceremony, including the President of Brazil, the King of Spain, and the Pope.
segments.zh: 几位重要的政要出席了开幕式，包括巴西总统、西班牙国王和教皇。

segments.en: There are going to be a lot of foreign dignitaries at the dinner.
segments.zh: 晚宴上会有很多外国政要。

segments.en: So basically we can understand that dignitaries are really important people, right?
segments.zh: 所以基本上我们可以理解，要人是非常重要的人，对吧？
重要的政治或宗教人物。

segments.en: All right, now our last word for language takeaway, palpable.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在我们的语言外卖的最后一个词，显而易见。

segments.en: When something is palpable, it's so strong you can feel it.
segments.zh: 当某件事是显而易见的时，它是如此强大，你可以感觉到它。

segments.en: Okay, so it's a very strong feeling.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这是一种非常强烈的感觉。

segments.en: Yeah, like the excitement was palpable or the fear was palpable.
segments.zh: 是的，就像兴奋是显而易见的，或者恐惧是显而易见的。
好吧，有趣的词，显而易见。

segments.en: Let's listen to our dialogue again and now let's try and listen to all these words we just talked about.
segments.zh: 让我们再听一次我们的对话，现在让我们试着听听我们刚刚谈到的所有这些话。

segments.en: This is Madeline Wright for BCC News reporting live from Washington, D.C., where very shortly the new president will deliver his inaugural address.
segments.zh: 这是来自华盛顿特区的 BCC News Reporting Live 的 Madeline Wright，新总统将在那里发表他的就职演说。

segments.en: Just moments ago, the president was sworn into office following the United States Constitution.
segments.zh: 总统刚刚依照《美国宪法》宣誓就职。

segments.en: The president swore an oath to faithfully execute the office of the presidency.
segments.zh: 他宣誓将忠实履行总统职责。

segments.en: And what exactly is going on now, Madeline?
segments.zh: 玛德琳现在到底发生了什么？

segments.en: Well, Tom, true to American tradition, the band has just played Hail to the Chief and the president has been honored with a 21-gun salute.
segments.zh: 汤姆，按照惯例，乐队刚刚演奏了《向统帅致敬》，还鸣放了二十一响礼炮向总统致敬。

segments.en: Now we're waiting for the president to take the stage and deliver his speech.
segments.zh: 现在我们正在等待总统上台发表他的演讲。

segments.en: Tom is like the who's who of the political world here on Capitol Hill with dignitaries representing several different countries.
segments.zh: 汤姆就像国会山上的政治世界名人录一样，政要代表几个不同的国家。

segments.en: What's the mood on the ground like, Madeline?
In a word, the mood here is electric.
segments.zh: 一句话，现场气氛热烈非凡。

segments.en: The excitement in the air is palpable.
segments.zh: 空气中洋溢的兴奋之情几乎触手可及。

segments.en: I've never seen a larger crowd here on Capitol Hill.
segments.zh: 我从没见过国会山上聚集这么多人。

segments.en: The audience is shouting, crying and embracing each other.
segments.zh: 观众们互相大喊大叫、哭泣和拥抱。

segments.en: On this, a most historic day, you can feel the hope and the excitement in the air.
segments.zh: 在这个最具历史意义的日子里，你可以感受到空气中的希望和兴奋。

segments.en: The 20th of January will go down in history as the...
segments.zh: 一月二十日将作为……载入史册。

segments.en: Oh, Tom, it looks like the president is about to begin.
segments.zh: 哦，汤姆，看起来总统即将开始。

segments.en: My fellow Americans, I stand before you today.
segments.zh: 我的美国同胞，我今天站在你们面前。

segments.en: Okay, so if you noticed in our dialogue, we have some really interesting phrases there.
segments.zh: 好的，如果您在我们的对话中注意到，我们有一些非常有趣的短语。

segments.en: So I think it's time for us to take a look at Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以我认为是时候让我们看看 Fluency Builder 了。

segments.en: On Fluency Builder today, we're going to be looking at three phrases that are very interesting because we can change them a little bit and form different patterns.
segments.zh: 今天在 Flueny Builder 上，我们将研究三个非常有趣的短语，因为我们可以稍微改变它们并形成不同的模式。

segments.en: So the first phrase we have is, in a word.
segments.zh: 所以我们有的第一个短语是，在一个词中。

segments.en: We use this expression when we want to describe something in one word.
segments.zh: 当我们想用一个词来描述某事时，我们使用这个表达式。

segments.en: We've got examples of how you could use this phrase.
segments.zh: 我们有如何使用这个短语的例子。

segments.en: In a word, the situation is serious.
Okay, so in a word, this podcast is...
Okay, let's look at our second phrase today.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们看看我们今天的第二个短语。

segments.en: So this is a really common phrase.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常普遍的短语。

segments.en: I'm sure you guys have heard it.
Yeah, basically something that is really important that everyone will remember for a very long time.
segments.zh: 是的，基本上每个人都会记住很长时间的东西非常重要。

segments.en: Let's look at this pattern with a few examples.
segments.zh: 让我们用几个例子来看看这个模式。

segments.en: This is going to go down in history as the worst disaster the world has ever seen.
segments.zh: 这将成为历史上最严重的灾难，这是世界上最严重的灾难。

segments.en: He'll go down in history as the best president we've ever had.
segments.zh: 他将成为我们有史以来最好的总统。

segments.en: This day will go down in history.
Okay, so as you can see, the pattern is we're using a superlative.
segments.zh: 好的，正如您所看到的，模式是我们使用的是最高级的。

segments.en: And our final phrase in putting it together is...
segments.zh: 我们把它放在一起的最后一句话是...

segments.en: So obviously you can change this one up a little bit, hey?
segments.zh: 所以很明显你可以稍微改变一下，嘿？

segments.en: You can say my fellow co-workers.
So basically fellow just means like dear.
segments.zh: 所以基本上同胞只是意味着像亲爱的。

segments.en: So we looked at some great vocabulary and phrases and now let's talk a little bit about these American traditions when electing a new president.
segments.zh: 所以我们看了一些很棒的词汇和短语，现在让我们在选举新总统时谈谈这些美国传统。

segments.en: Today in the studio we have JP who's joining us.
segments.zh: 今天在工作室里，我们有 JP 加入我们。

segments.en: And he's going to be talking to us about these traditions.
segments.zh: 他将与我们谈论这些传统。

segments.en: What are we going to talk about?
The 21 gun salute is the military salute where they say, and now we will have the 21 gun salute.
segments.zh: 21 枪敬礼是他们说的军事敬礼，现在我们将有 21 枪敬礼。

segments.en: So 21 soldiers with their rifles, they go, and they all shoot them off at the same time.
segments.zh: 所以21名士兵拿着步枪走了，他们都同时开枪。

segments.en: I think it's a sign of respect, hey?
segments.zh: 我认为这是尊重的标志，嘿？

segments.en: Well, I think in Europe they would do a cannon or something.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为在欧洲，他们会做大炮什么的。

segments.en: Maybe our European listeners know the answer to this.
segments.zh: 也许我们的欧洲听众知道这个问题的答案。

segments.en: And what about this song Hail to the Chief?
segments.zh: 那么这首歌向酋长致敬呢？

segments.en: Do you know anything about that?
I do not know anything about it except that it's a march and I think it's Souza.
segments.zh: 我对它一无所知，除了它是游行，我认为它是 Souza。

segments.en: I think John Philip Souza wrote it.
segments.zh: 我认为约翰·菲利普·索萨写了它。

segments.en: And whenever the president walks into a room, they play that song.
segments.zh: 每当总统走进一个房间时，他们就会播放那首歌。

segments.en: And I played it once for President Bush, the first one.
segments.zh: 我为布什总统玩过一次，第一个。

segments.en: And my marching band had to play that song for him.
segments.zh: 我的军乐队不得不为他演奏那首歌。

segments.en: Oh my God, JP, you're like famous.
This was back in like 1986 or something.
segments.zh: 这回到了 1986 年之类的地方。

segments.en: Was that even an election year?
Well, you did play for the president, so you know.
segments.zh: 好吧，你确实为总统效力，所以你知道的。

segments.en: So JP, do you have any other sort of traditional things that happen when the president becomes the president?
segments.zh: 那么JP，当总统成为总统时，你还有其他类型的传统事情吗？

segments.en: Well, I can tell you that Jimmy Carter, you know, when he was elected president, his motorcade was going down Pennsylvania Avenue and he stopped the car and got out.
segments.zh: 好吧，我可以告诉你，吉米·卡特，你知道，当他当选总统时，他的车队正在沿着宾夕法尼亚大道驶下，他停下了车下车。

segments.en: He wanted to walk down Pennsylvania Avenue.
segments.zh: 他想走在宾夕法尼亚大道。

segments.en: He wanted to walk down the, you know, down the street.
segments.zh: 他想走在街上，你知道的。

segments.en: And I think it made the Secret Service insane.
segments.zh: 我认为这让特勤局发疯了。

segments.en: Maybe the car smelled bad or something.
segments.zh: 也许这辆车闻起来很糟糕或什么的。

segments.en: I think that is my memory of it.
segments.zh: 我想这是我对它的记忆。

segments.en: I might be confusing with the West Wing, but I'm not sure.
segments.zh: 我可能会与西翼混淆，但我不确定。

segments.en: But when the president walks, it's a big deal.
segments.zh: 但当总统走了，这很重要。

segments.en: So JP, do you do anything special for the inauguration ceremony?
segments.zh: 那么JP，你为就职典礼做了什么特别的事情吗？

segments.en: I always take the day off to watch.
I love, you know, the swearing in ceremony, the ritual of it, the speech.
segments.zh: 我喜欢，你知道，在仪式中宣誓，仪式，演讲。

segments.en: All right, everyone, we're out of time.
segments.zh: 好吧，大家，我们没时间了。

segments.en: I hope you enjoyed this political lesson.
segments.zh: 我希望你喜欢这个政治课。

segments.en: I hope you have a happy inauguration day.
segments.zh: 我希望你有一个快乐的就职日。

segments.en: We're definitely going to take the day off to watch it with JP.
segments.zh: 我们肯定会休息一天与 JP 一起观看。

segments.en: And hopefully you guys can too.
